payload.name: Include preference memories for recently-finished-activity queries
payload.description: When a question asks what someone just finished reading, watching, playing, or otherwise recently completed, do not restrict memory_kinds to 'event'; include 'preference' and 'state' because completed favorites are often stored as preference memories.
content: If a user asks what a person recently finished or just completed (e.g., a book, show, game, project), set memory_kinds to include both 'event' and 'preference' (or omit the filter), because such completed items are often stored as preference memories rather than event memories.

When the question combines a completion verb ('finished', 'just read', 'completed') with a concrete date, do not limit retrieval only to event memories on that date; run an additional search without a memory_kinds restriction or with 'preference' included so that preference memories with a matching world_start can surface.

Before answering 'no information available' for a completed-activity question, check whether any retrieved preference or state memory explicitly states the completed item, even if no event memory matches.

solves: Diagnosed failure: an agent asked what book a person just finished reading on a specific date, restricted memory_kinds to 'event', and missed the preference memory that contained the completed book. The abstract mechanism is over-restricting memory_kinds to event for completion queries, even though recently completed activities and items are often stored as preference memories. This rule applies to any future question about a recently finished or completed activity/artifact and prevents premature 'no information' answers.
